title: Schroedinger libschroedinger through 1.0.11 contains a divide by zero vulnerability that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying a zero… (CVE-2026-112054)
description: Schroedinger libschroedinger versions up to 1.0.11 contain a divide by zero vulnerability. This flaw allows attackers to cause a denial of service by crashing applications when a zero value is supplied for slice_bytes_denom or slice count in a Dirac stream. The vulnerability triggers a SIGFPE signal during parsing of crafted low-delay pictures.
aiSummary: The vulnerability in libschroedinger through version 1.0.11 is a divide by zero error (CWE-369) that occurs when an attacker supplies a zero value for slice_bytes_denom or slice count in a Dirac stream. This crafted input is parsed by the functions schro_decoder_parse_transform_parameters and schro_decoder_parse_lowdelay_transform_data, which leads to a SIGFPE (floating point exception) and crashes the application, resulting in denial of service. The CVSS 3.1 score is 5.5 (medium severity) with vector AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H, indicating local attack vector, low complexity, no privileges required, user interaction required, unchanged scope, no confidentiality or integrity impact, and high availability impact.
aiImpact: Successful exploitation causes a denial of service by crashing the affected application through a divide by zero error. There is no impact on confidentiality or integrity. The attack requires local access and user interaction.
